sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Accession**: Jahandar Shah ascended the throne after defeating his brothers in the War of Succession (1712) with the support of **Zulfiqar Khan**.
• **Kingmaker Influence**: His reign represents the first instance where a powerful noble (Wazir) dictated imperial policy, effectively reducing the Emperor to a figurehead.
• **Fiscal Policy**: Introduction of **Ijarah** (revenue farming) to address the acute financial crisis, which led to the exploitation of the peasantry.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The reign lasted only 11 months, highlighting the extreme political instability and the rapid turnover of power in the 18th-century Mughal court.

items.definition: A system of revenue farming where the right to collect land revenue was auctioned to the highest bidder, leading to increased peasant oppression.
The powerful Wazir who acted as the 'Kingmaker' for Jahandar Shah, attempting to stabilize the empire through administrative reforms.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Conciliation Policy**: Attempted to reconcile with Rajput rulers (Ajit Singh and Jai Singh) to maintain territorial integrity.
• **Chauth and Sardeshmukhi**: Granted these rights to the Marathas to pacify the Deccan frontier.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Constant threat from Farrukhsiyar (nephew) and internal court factionalism.
• **Solutions**: The failure to curb the Sayyid Brothers ultimately led to his deposition and execution.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'J-Z-I' (Jahandar, Zulfiqar, Ijarah).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Jahandar Shah was supported by Zulfiqar Khan and introduced the Ijarah system.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Ijarah' system with the 'Jagirdari' system. Ijarah is revenue farming, whereas Jagirdari is the assignment of land revenue for military service.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Patrimonial Absolutism' to describe the shift from institutional governance to personal factionalism under Jahandar Shah.

keyTakeaways: Jahandar Shah's reign marks the transition from Mughal autocracy to the era of Kingmakers.
The introduction of Ijarah signaled the beginning of the economic decline of the Mughal agrarian system.
The reliance on court favorites like Lal Kunwar undermined the legitimacy of the Mughal throne.
